item.title: Marine heat waves boost coastal CO₂ uptake by 11%, analysis finds
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Marine heat waves are a consequence of climate change and are increasingly altering marine and coastal regions worldwide. An international study led by the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon now shows that many coastal seas absorb more CO₂ from the atmosphere during these extreme events than under normal conditions. The effect is particularly pronounced in polar and subpolar shelf seas of the Northern Hemisphere, where sea ice is declining as temperatures rise.

item.title: The American “cheetah” wasn’t a cheetah at all
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — The extinct “American cheetah” was not really a cheetah at all, but a puma relative with an unexpectedly flexible lifestyle. Fossils from the Yukon suggest northern populations survived partly by eating fish, possibly including salmon, while southern cats hunted on land.

item.title: Early statin use linked to 15% lower dementia risk
item.description: [Diabetes & Kidney Disease] Keyword: type 2 diabetes — Starting statins soon after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis may do more than protect the heart. In a nationwide Danish study of more than 132,000 people, those who began statin treatment within a year of diagnosis had a 15% lower relative risk of developing dementia over 10 years compared with those who did not start statins.

item.title: Your gut microbiome may be more contagious than scientists thought
item.description: [Diabetes & Kidney Disease] Keyword: type 2 diabetes — Scientists have found evidence that some gut bacterial populations can spread rapidly between people and across continents, suggesting the microbiome may be more transmissible than previously thought. The research also revealed hidden bacterial groups associated with aging, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, and type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Ozempic and Wegovy may have an unexpected mental health benefit
item.description: [Diabetes & Kidney Disease] Keyword: GLP-1 — Semaglutide, the drug behind Ozempic and Wegovy, may have benefits that extend well beyond weight loss and diabetes. In a large Swedish study of nearly 15,000 people with bipolar disorder, its use was linked to a 21% lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization. Researchers think effects on inflammation and brain-related biological pathways could help stabilize mood, though other GLP-1 drugs did not show the same association.
